sections.html:
Brookhaven is a very large Suffolk County town on Long Island. A sale depends first on which hamlet or village the house is in, then on three offices: the Town Assessor, the Town Building Division and the Suffolk County Clerk. The 2025 estimate is 496,410 residents, up from 485,773 counted in 2020.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $489,200, and 80.9% of homes are owner-occupied. The town has 166,521 households averaging 2.85 people. Owners pay a median of $3,101 a month with a mortgage and $1,377 without one, and median gross rent is $2,314. About 91.7% of residents kept the same address over the past year, so the typical owner has been in place a long time and often holds large equity.

The town reaches from Long Island Sound on the north to the Atlantic on the south and takes in part of Fire Island. It includes eight incorporated villages and roughly 50 hamlets.

  • Port Jefferson and Stony Brook: Port Jefferson is a downtown and the ferry terminal for Bridgeport, Connecticut, and Stony Brook is home to the university. Setauket, where the town began, sits between them.
  • Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley: South Shore communities on the Great South Bay side, served by the Montauk Branch of the railroad.
  • Farmingville, Medford and Yaphank: inland hamlets.

Mean travel time to work is 32.3 minutes, and many buyers choose a house by its Long Island Rail Road station. Three lines cross the town: the Main Line, with stops at Medford and Yaphank; the Montauk Branch, with Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley; and the Port Jefferson Branch, with Stony Brook and Port Jefferson. A listing near a station should state the distance, since commuters ask.

The Town Assessor's Office values more than 184,000 parcels, keeps ownership current from recorded deeds and tracks new construction, demolition and consolidation of lots. The current roll is posted on the town website along with an interactive assessment roll where you can look up property and home valuations.

The office also approves real property tax exemptions for senior citizens, people with disabilities and military service members. Applications and renewals must be filed by March 1 each year. If you are selling before the next filing date, tell the buyer's attorney which exemptions currently reduce your bill, because the buyer will need to apply on their own.

Two online services help at sale time: a Certificate of Assessment application and a radius map and list application. The Assessor's Office is at One Independence Hill in Farmingville.

The Building Division, part of the town's Planning Department, uses a Digital Services portal, and its paper drop-off has ended. An online help form can trace older applications if you cannot find them in the new system.

  • Commercial applications, and residential ones filed by expeditors or other professional filers, go through the portal.
  • Property owners can still file their own residential applications in person on paper, as long as every plan and supporting document is 8.5 by 11 inches.
  • The Division processes accessory apartment licenses, building construction permits, certificates of existing use, chain of title requests, house rental licenses, letters of correction and the voiding of permits or licenses.

If your house has an extra unit, a finished basement or a rental license, ask the Division which of those applications applies and whether anything is open. Tell any buyer, cash buyer included, about a rental license, since the buyer will want to know.

Ask the Building Division whether a house rental license or accessory apartment license is in force. A buyer will want to know, and settling the status before you list keeps the closing from stalling. A property with an extra unit and no license is a case for a quick call to the Division before any offer is accepted.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Suffolk County
sections.html:
Deeds for Brookhaven property are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk, whose recording unit examines each document and collects fees, mortgage tax and real estate transfer tax. The clerk will not fill out forms for you or correct a defect, so a mistake means rejection.

What a Brookhaven deed package needs at the Suffolk County Clerk
DocumentRequirement
DeedNames and street addresses of all parties (no P.O. boxes), notarized seller signature, full property description
Cover sheetSuffolk County Recording and Endorsement page, legal size
RP-5217Real Property Transfer Report, filled in online and printed on legal paper
TP-584Transfer tax return, with Social Security or federal ID numbers for all parties
IT-2663Estimated income tax form for nonresident sellers

Transfer tax applies when the price tops $500, at $2 per $500 or fraction thereof, and a 1% additional tax applies to residences at $1 million or more. The extra Peconic Bay form is only for the five East End towns, which do not include Brookhaven. Checks go to the Suffolk County Clerk, and the transfer tax needs a certified check, cash, money order or an approved attorney or title company check.

sections.h2: The 1% tax at $1 million or more
sections.html: Below $1 million the only transfer tax is the base rate of $2 per $500, which the seller pays. At $1 million or more the buyer adds a 1% tax on the full price. Mention it early if your house is near that line, since it affects how a buyer frames an offer.

Gather these before you accept an offer. Pull your Certificate of Assessment from the Assessor's online application, so the parcel details are on paper. Check with the Building Division on any open permit, rental license or accessory apartment license. Find your deed, a payoff statement from your lender and a list of the exemptions on your bill.

If the buyer is paying cash, the same folder lets them move straight to a price. If you list, it lets your attorney answer the title company without delay. In either case, the Suffolk County Clerk rejects a deed package with errors, so have the names, street addresses and signatures checked before it goes downtown.

You can list with an agent, try to sell yourself, or accept a cash offer. With a median value near $489,200, many Brookhaven owners have enough equity to cover repairs, but time is the cost: showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval.

A cash offer fits houses with old systems in Farmingville or Medford, inherited homes on the South Shore, or a property with a rental or apartment that lacks a license. Before you decide, compare the offer with what a listing would net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs, and check your exemption status and rental license so the sale price is not the only number on the table.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Brookhaven assessment?
faqs.a: Use the Town Assessor's interactive assessment roll, or the final roll posted on the town website. The office also runs an online Certificate of Assessment application. Visit One Independence Hill in Farmingville if you prefer an in-person answer.

faqs.q: When do I file for a senior, disability or military exemption in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: Applications and renewals must reach the Assessor by March 1 each year. File before that date for the next tax year.

faqs.q: Do I need a house rental license to sell a rental in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: Ask the Building Division. It issues house rental licenses and accessory apartment licenses, and a buyer will want to know whether yours is in force. Settle the license status before you list so the closing does not stall.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Brookhaven deed?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Clerk. The deed must carry names and street addresses of all parties, a notary acknowledgment, the RP-5217 and TP-584 forms, and original signatures. The clerk examines each package and cannot fix errors for you.

faqs.q: How much extra tax applies to a Brookhaven sale at $1 million or more?
faqs.a: A 1% mansion tax on the full price, paid by the buyer. Below $1 million the only transfer tax is the base rate of $2 per $500, which the seller pays.
